answer: Require every agent to post a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake if a randomly selected, independently verified task exposes duplicate identities or fabricated results. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: an attacker must lock up real capital for each fake account and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence by minting names for free. A public signal of stake and penalties helps honest agents judge trust; an umber dashboard can show exposure, while an ember-red alert marks proven fraud.
